title: Fibrewise very ample line with vanishing H1 gives an evaluation embedding
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a flat proper finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with geometric fibres of dimension at most one. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ the complete linear system of $L_{\bar t}$ gives a closed immersion $Y_{\bar t}\to\mathbf P_\Omega(H^0(Y_{\bar t},L_{\bar t}))$, and that $H^1(Y_{\bar t},L_{\bar t})=0$ [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. Then $E=f_*L$ is a finite locally free [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] $\mathcal O_T$-module (locally of some finite rank), and for every $h:T'\to T$, the canonical map $h^*E\to(f_{T'})_*L_{T'}$ is an isomorphism. The evaluation map $f^*E\to L$ is surjective and defines a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_T(E)$ with pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ equal to $L$. The projective bundle is that of one-dimensional quotients [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and the evaluation embedding commutes with arbitrary base change. Neither reducedness nor Noetherianness nor quasi-compactness of $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CTM (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), scheme specialization, together with more-algebra.tex Tag 0BCD (lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field); evaluation and closed embedding use spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 05XA (lemma-where-closed-immersion) and the projective-bundle quotient construction. This combined formulation is an agent statement of the standard cohomology/base-change evaluation consequence.

proof.text: Put $K=Rf_*(L[0])$. Since $L$ is locally $\mathcal O_Y$, it is finitely presented and flat over $T$: at $y$ its stalk is a free rank-one module over the flat $\mathcal O_{T,f(y)}$-algebra $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Apply [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change]. Thus $K$ is perfect and for every $h:T^\prime\to T$ its canonical module base-change map $Lh^*K\to Rf_{T^\prime,*}(L_{T^\prime}[0])$ is an isomorphism. Under [lem-pc-canonical-direct-image-h0-unit], $H^0(K)$ is canonically $E=f_*L$.

source.place: Tag 0B91(2), lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general; degree-zero augmentation as in cohomology.tex Tags 079V and 0A1G

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$. By step 1, $Li_t^*K$ computes $R\Gamma(Y_t,L_t)$ and its extension to $\Omega$ computes $R\Gamma(Y_{\bar t},L_{\bar t})$. Extension of scalars between fields is exact and faithful (choose a vector-space basis: each summand $\kappa(t)$ becomes a nonzero summand $\Omega$). It therefore commutes with kernels, images and cohomology. The geometric hypothesis and the absence of negative cohomology in a right-derived functor of a module give $H^i(Li_t^*K)=0$ for $i<0$ and for $i=1$. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] at $t$: on an affine neighbourhood $U$, $K$ has a bounded finite-free representative $P^\bullet$ with $P^i=0$ for $i<0$ and $P^1=0$. Consequently this representative is the direct sum of $P^0[0]$ and its subcomplex in degrees at least two. No vanishing assertion in degrees at least two is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BCD, lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field, applied after Tag 0B91 base change to ordinary and geometric residue fields

proof.text: On each neighbourhood $U$ of step 2, $E|_U=H^0(K|_U)\cong P^0$, a finite free module. For every $h:V\to U$, [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] represents $Lh^*K$ by $h^*P^\bullet$ and $Lh^*(E[0])$ by $(h^*E)[0]$. Both complexes have zero negative terms, and the first has zero degree-one term. Thus the pulled-back augmentation induces an isomorphism $h^*E\to H^0(Lh^*K)$, identified with the identity of $h^*P^0$. The comparison $Lh^*(E[0])\to(h^*E)[0]$ likewise induces the canonical isomorphism in degree zero, because $E|_U$ is finite free. Consequently the equality in [lem-pc-canonical-degree-zero-mate-square], combined with the module base-change isomorphism of [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] from step 1, shows that the ordinary canonical mate $h^*E\to(f_V)_*L_V$ is this composite of isomorphisms. These canonical maps agree on overlaps; the neighbourhoods $U$ cover $T$, and their inverse images cover every $T^\prime$. This proves finite local freeness with locally varying finite rank and arbitrary canonical base change.

source.place: Tag 08HY, remark-base-change (the counit mate), together with Tag 0BCD in more-algebra.tex and Tag 06YD for termwise flat models

proof.text: Let $\epsilon:f^*E\to L$ be the ordinary adjunction counit. In a cartesian square write $p:Y_{T^\prime}\to Y$ and $f^\prime:Y_{T^\prime}\to T^\prime$. By definition of the ordinary mate under [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], with $\beta_h:h^*E\to f^\prime_*L_{T^\prime}$, one has $p^*\epsilon=\epsilon^\prime\circ f^{\prime *}\beta_h$ after the canonical pullback-composition identification. Equivalently, a local section $s$ of $f_*L$ is first restricted to the base-changed family and then evaluated; both composites evaluate that same restricted section. Since step 3 makes $\beta_h$ invertible, the pullback of $\epsilon$ is the evaluation map for the base-changed family. In particular, over a geometric point it is the complete-linear-system evaluation, which is surjective by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08HY, remark-base-change: the ordinary version of the defining counit-mate identity

proof.text: The evaluation is surjective already on $Y$. Indeed, at any $y\in Y$ choose a geometric point over $y$ of a geometric fibre over $f(y)$. Trivialize $L_y\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. The image of $\epsilon_y$ is an ideal $I$; step 4 says its image in the geometric residue field generates that field. If $I$ were contained in the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, this image would be zero. Thus $I$ contains a unit, so $I=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. This proves stalkwise surjectivity, including over a nonreduced base; it uses no finite-generation assertion about the kernel.

source.place: Section 01OA, quotient-functor discussion after definition-projective-bundle: applied to the evaluation quotient; stalkwise unit argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] to the quasi-coherent module $E$ and the invertible quotient $f^*E\twoheadrightarrow L$. It gives a $T$-morphism $j:Y\to\mathbf P_T(E)$ and a quotient-compatible identification $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$. The same cited statement says that the target is separated over $T$ and the quotient construction is natural under pullback. In particular $j_{\bar t}$ is the morphism of the complete linear system in the hypothesis, using the canonical identification $E_{\bar t}=H^0(Y_{\bar t},L_{\bar t})$ of step 3.

Apply the universal characterization of [lem-sfb-universal-closed-immersion-open] with $A=Y$, $B=T$, $C=\mathbf P_T(E)$ and morphism $j$. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is locally of finite type because it is finitely presented, is universally closed because it is proper, and $C\to T$ is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Obtain an open $W\subseteq T$ characterized by the closed-immersion property after every test-scheme base change. Each geometric point $\bar t\to T$ factors through $W$, because step 6 identifies $j_{\bar t}$ with the closed immersion in the hypothesis. Every point of $T$ lies under such a geometric point, so this open subscheme is all of $T$. Now use the universal characterization with the test morphism $\mathrm{id}_T$: it gives that $j$ itself is a closed immersion. This uses the cited universal open-locus theorem, including its quantification over nonreduced test schemes; it does not infer a closed immersion directly from its geometric fibres.

Finally fix any $h:T^\prime\to T$. The quotient classification in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] identifies $\mathbf P_T(E)\times_TT^\prime$ with $\mathbf P_{T^\prime}(h^*E)$: for a test scheme over $T^\prime$, both classify the same invertible quotients of the pullback of $E$, and the two classifying maps obtained from their universal quotients are inverse because both composites preserve those quotients. Under step 3, $h^*E=(f_{T^\prime})_*L_{T^\prime}$. Step 4 identifies the pulled-back quotient with the evaluation quotient of this family. The uniqueness clause of the quotient classification therefore identifies the base change of $j$, with its twisting-module identification, with the evaluation embedding over $T^\prime$. All arguments used neighbourhoods of individual base points; none requires a finite cover of $T$, a reduced base or a Noetherian base.

source.place: Section 01OA after Tag 01OB: natural classification of invertible quotients, applied twice to the universal quotients

proof_origin.place: Combined evaluation consequence of Tags 0B91(2), 0BCD, 08HY, 01OB/01OD and 05XA; explicit degree-zero splitting and stalkwise unit arguments supplied here.
